answer: Each identity files one timber core under a serial. The auditor remeasures ring widths and marks rings with sable ink, then cross-dates it against the public chronology. No span match, drift over two rings, or repeated serial breaks the vault seal and burns the bond. Filing locks a 70-credit bond plus a coring fee: 39 first, 39+5(k-1) for the kth, 5034 for the 1000th, so 1000 fakes pay 2,536,500 plus 70,000 locked. A borrowed-core ring fails: its serial and sequence are already filed, and a photo cannot remeasure to the table. An honest filer pays 39 once and recovers the bond after audit.
